summaries.Good news: Real human progress is unfolding: women's baseball returns after 70 years, coral reefs recover from bleaching with natural help, and communities are solving water scarcity through grassroots restoration. These aren't headlines—they're turning points.
summaries.Ideas: AI is reshaping everything from how companies think about carbon footprints to how individuals approach job security, while emerging science reveals unexpected biological frontiers like organoid intelligence and schizophrenia's genetic roots.
summaries.Technology: Autonomous systems are reaching major milestones (AI air combat), classic products are gaining smart capabilities (Casio's step-counting watch), and infrastructure is breaking records (the Gordie Howe bridge), signaling how technology integrates into everyday life.
summaries.Design: From mirrored pavilions that play with light to folding chairs rethinking compromise, designers are tackling real problems—accessibility, material waste, public space connection—while questioning whether familiar objects like chairs and washbasins need complete reimagining.

items.title: Pro Women’s Baseball Resumes for First Time Since 1954: A League of Their Own is BACK!
items.snippet: Almost eight decades after she last played baseball, Maybelle Blair returned to the diamond—in a wheelchair—to inaugurate the new women’s US baseball league. items.line: After nearly 70 years away, professional women's baseball returns with a living legend inaugurating the new league—a full-circle moment for American sports and gender equity.

items.line: The Great Barrier Reef's recovery from mass bleaching shows that even degraded ecosystems can bounce back when conditions align—a rare bright spot in climate reality.

items.line: Anthropic will embed invisible watermarks in all AI-generated text, setting a new transparency standard that could reshape how society identifies synthetic content.

items.title: AI Could Help Fossil Fuel Companies Create More Emissions
